guide: Open the Start sheet and type your school, your name, the class and the weight of each assessment type in the yellow cells.
Set your grade scale, the late penalty, the retake cap, the reading goal and the alerts for averages, absences and missing work.
List your students on the Students sheet with a parent or guardian and a phone number with the country code.
Add each homework, quiz, project and test on the Assignments sheet with its maximum points and its standard or unit.
Enter scores on the Scores sheet, one row per student per assignment. Mark late, missing or excused work, and add retake points when a student redoes it.
Take attendance on the Attendance sheet: one row per student per day.
Log merit points and issues on the Behavior Log, reading on the Reading Log and every call or message on Parent Contacts.
Open a support plan for a student who needs extra help, with a goal and a review date.
Book parent meetings on Parent Meetings and send the reminder from the same row.
Plan your lessons on the Lesson Plan sheet; print the Cover Plan for a substitute teacher when you are away.
Record books and devices you lend on Loans, and what you buy for the class on Classroom Spending.
Put duties, meetings, deadlines and trips on the Calendar.
Write one comment per grade on the Comment Bank; each student's comment appears on the progress report.
Check the Class Dashboard and the Charts every week, and send ready messages from the Students sheet.
Print the Progress Report, Student File, Meeting Letter, Permission Slip or Certificate by choosing a student, a trip or a lesson at the top.

listing.description:
Run your class from one Excel workbook: a weighted gradebook, attendance, missing work, support plans, reading, parent contacts and meetings, lesson plans, loans and your own classroom spending, with every average, grade and alert worked out for you.

Most teachers keep grades in one file, attendance on paper and parent calls in their head. Missing work and falling results are noticed too late, and nobody adds up what you spend on the class. ClassMark puts it all in one place.

WHAT IT DOES
• Weighted term grade from homework, quizzes, projects and tests, with your weights and A-F scale
• Late work loses your penalty, a better retake counts up to your cap, missing work counts as zero
• Early warning: students at risk, and a warning when the 30-day average falls
• Attendance rate and absences of the last 30 days for every student
• 11 ready WhatsApp messages: absence, missing work, good news, falling results, reading, meetings, loans, support plans
• Support plans with goals, review dates, alerts and a checklist
• Reading log against your monthly goal, merit points and a behavior log
• Report card comments filled in from your own comment bank
• Parent meetings with reminders, a preparation checklist and what you agreed
• Calculators: score needed on the final, grade curve, marking time, rubric scorer, grade converter, standard mastery
• Printables: progress report, student file, meeting letter, permission slip, certificate, cover plan for a substitute teacher
• Loans of books and devices, classroom spending and what the school owes you, and a calendar of duties, meetings and deadlines
• Dashboard and charts: class average, attendance, missing work, reading, support plans, contacts and spending

YOU RECEIVE a ZIP with the workbook in 15 languages and an English copy filled with sample data. Standard .xlsx files for Microsoft Excel and LibreOffice. No macros, no subscription. Licence for one teacher.

messages.text: Hello {guardian}, {name} was absent from class today. Absences in the last 30 days: {abs30}. Please let me know if there is anything I should know.
Hello {guardian}, {name} has {missing} missing assignments in my class. Could you help {name} hand them in this week? Thank you.
Hello {guardian}, some good news: {name} has worked really well in class this week. I wanted you to know.
Hello {guardian}, I would like to meet you to talk about how {name} is doing in class. Which day suits you?
Hello {guardian}, {name}'s grade in my class is {grade} so far this term. I will send the full progress report soon.
Hello {guardian}, {name}'s results in the last few weeks are lower than usual. Could we work on this together? I am happy to talk.
Hello {guardian}, {name} read for {reading_month} minutes this month. Thank you for reading together at home!
Hello {guardian}, I need to tell you about something that happened in class with {name} today. Please call me when you can.
Hello {guardian}, a reminder of our meeting about {s_name} on {date} at {time}. See you then!
Hello {guardian}, {s_name} borrowed {item} from our class. Please help {s_name} bring it back by {due}. Thank you.
Hello {guardian}, an update on {s_name}'s support plan: {progress}. Next review: {review}.

documents.title: Invitation to a parent meeting
paragraphs: I would like to meet you to talk about how {col:students.name} is doing in class.
In the last 30 days {col:students.name} was absent {col:students.abs30} times and has {col:students.missing} missing assignments. The current grade is {col:students.grade}.
Please reply with a day and time that suits you. Thank you for your support.
